text:
mari: Heads-up — saw a latency/regression signal after the picker tweak last night. On sm94, INT4+FP8 stack picks are flipping for short sequences (~8-32) and causing cold-start tail latency to spike. attaching short profile and logs.

sam: ugh. is this the pinball-sampler change from yesterday?

mari: yeah, the new 'pinball sampler' that biases toward int4 for cost savings. It uses a lightweight warmth score to prefer kernels that were recently hot. problem is the warmth estimator is noisy for KV-cold requests so it sometimes picks the wrong execution path then falls back mid-request => extra copies and long kernels.

ryan: can you paste the flame or the pprof snapshot? curious where the time is going.

mari: sure — snippet from perf-bot run 12345:
```
# short seq (16) cold KV
shard0: choose_kernel -> int4_path_v2 (warmth=0.12)
kernel_launch: stalling memcpy and quant-dequant fallback
KVcache: miss -> synchronous load (1.2ms)
int4_path_v2: kernel runtime 2.8ms + 1.1ms memcpy fallback
finalize -> extra memcpy -> total 5.1ms
# older path (fp8_fallback) would have been 2.2ms steady
```

mari: TL;DR — sampler's bias caused an expensive flip when KV was cold. The 'pessimistic fallback' triggers heavy memcpy.

sam: so two levers: 1) make warmth score conservative for short seqs, 2) add a KV-cold override that forces conservative kernel picks until cache warms. 

ryan: i tried a quick patch that adds a per-request kv_warmth flag (0..1) computed from KV hit rate in the last N requests per shard. If kv_warmth < 0.2, we prefer FP8/int8 stable paths for seq<64. Ran a canary on a subset and 99p latency dropped ~18% for cold flows.

mari: nice. can you share the config diff?

ryan: config snippet we used in canary:
```json
{"pinball_sampler": {"warmth_window": 32, "warmth_threshold_short_seq": 0.2, "short_seq_max": 64, "fallback_hysteresis_ms": 5}}
```

sam: how did this affect overall cost? any increase in token-ms?

ryan: negligible on hot flows (<0.5%); cold flows improved performance and reduced replays. overall cost delta ~+0.2% but 99p latency wins were worth it for the customer SLAs.

mari: we should also add a small delay to sampling decisions for the very first token to avoid flip during the request. e.g., don't allow a kernel change after first launch unless path error. keeps state machine simpler.

devops: perf-bot result: job 12345 uploaded to s3://redwood-profiles/2177777777/12345.pb.gz, flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/s/2177777777/12345

perf-bot: automated analysis: probable root causes — (1) sampler bias mis-estimate on small-window warmth, (2) KV synchronous loads dominating short seq, (3) memcpy fallback cost on int4->fp8 switch. Confidence: high.

sam: next steps: (A) roll kv_warmth short-seq guard to mainline with an opt-in flag, (B) add an additional penalty term in pinball warmth for KV misses, (C) instrument to emit a "path_flip" metric (counts flips per request), (D) add unit test that simulates cold KV + short seq to prevent regressions.

mari: i'll draft the PR with tests and the metric. assigning to @ryan for the canary rollout and @devops for metric pipeline. thanks all :thumbsup:

ryan: will do the canary tomorrow morning and post results. if stable we'll flip the flag off in two weeks.

mari: filing a short postmortem note on the regression board. linking this thread.

sam: nice triage — good call catching the sampler/KV interaction early.
